requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`.

**Direct references (subject, contributed source, acknowledgment)**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` has the subject cite `terms.unit`. It asserts that exactly two definition inputs appear in the mandatory inputs.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_inputs_can_read_untracked_declarations_and_terms]` has a contributed source reference `terms.ready`. It asserts that `terms.ready` is supplied as a definition input.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[acknowledgment_only_terms_are_supplied_and_validated_without_implementation_reads]` has a `{fixme}` body reference `terms.boundary`. It asserts four things:
  - The prompt contains the declarations' text ("A unit." and "at the limit.").
  - The implementation body is absent from the prompt.
  - No outline input is created.
  - Evidence validation fails if the definition input is missing ("expected exactly one definition input for terms.boundary, found 0").

**Transitive inclusion, no duplicates, and cycles**
- In the bundle test, `unit` and `value` reference each other, which is a cycle. Only the subject references `unit`, yet exactly two definitions are supplied. That shows the closure is transitive, deduplicated, and terminates.
- In the acknowledgment test, `boundary` depends on `unit`. A change to `unit` is detected as a changed `Definition` input, which shows the transitive dependency is recorded.
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted]` checks the transitive terms `terms.base` and `terms.value` and the exact definition text.

**Complete fenced declaration with phrase option**
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]` asserts that each definition's text begins with `:::{definition}` and that its second line starts with `:phrase: `.
- The exact-text assertions in `declaration_text_reaches_the_model_redacted` and `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` also cover the full declaration including the phrase line.

**Additional reads**
- The `mod.rs` test above drives `assess` with a `ReadingProvider`. The read of `fn[work]` introduces `terms.value`, which pulls in `terms.unit` through the cycle. The test asserts four things:
  - The recorded evidence inputs list `["terms.unit", "terms.value"]`, once each.
  - The second request contains the transitive text ("A unit of").
  - The first request does not contain that text.
  - The submission came after delivery.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` covers the same for item reads and line-range reads, and checks recording and deduplication.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` covers paged reads. The page that needs the term carries its definition, and delivery equals the page's inputs plus its definitions.

**Residual**
- No test puts a term only in a cited requirement's text. Mandatory-input terminology is computed by one shared dependency routine over all mandatory inputs, so there is no separate branch to test.

I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject, any contributed source, or an acknowledgment supplied
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs` MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
A file selected as a mandatory input MUST be visible under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`. A denied selection MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
:::{req} fixme_inputs
For a requirement or example assessment, the initial request MUST include every
valid named `{fixme}` reference to the subject found under
{cite}`requirements.references.discovery`, except a reference inside one of
the subject's sites under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, in this
form:
```text
Acknowledgment {
file: String,
item: String,
body: String,
issues: Array<{ reference: String, state: "open" | "closed" }>,
`file` and `item` MUST locate the containing source by project-relative path and
outline selector, using `<root>` for a whole file. `body` MUST contain the
reference's complete fenced commentary without its fences or source-comment
delimiters, including its option lines, redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. `issues` MUST give every distinct issue
its `:github:` lines name, in their order, with state supplied under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`. Acknowledgments MUST be ordered by
file and position in the file and MUST carry no line numbers or containing
implementation source.
The locations and bodies MUST be protected against staleness by the reference-set
digest under {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`; the acknowledgment MUST NOT
create an outline input merely to cover its containing source. Actual reads of
that source MUST still be recorded under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`. Sources MUST satisfy
{cite}`requirements.authoring.source_tools`; an inaccessible acknowledgment
MUST be reported before inference.
Terminology definitions referenced by an acknowledgment's body MUST contribute
their complete, transitive declarations to the mandatory input set under
{cite}`requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs` and MUST be recorded as
definition inputs. Only the acknowledgment's body MUST contribute these
dependencies; its containing implementation source MUST NOT be supplied merely
to discover them.
